definition: Accede means to agree to a request or proposal.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word accede. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know accede should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: After a year of petitions about the dangerous school corner, the city acceded and painted the crosswalk over spring break.
To consider a request is much milder than to accede to it — considering only weighs the ask, while accede means the resistance ended and the thing asked for was granted.
Consent stops short of accede — you can consent gladly on the spot, while accede means a holdout finally gave way.

Assent is formal agreement that a statement, plan, or opinion is sound — a nod of approval in a boardroom. You assent to ideas; you accede to requests made of you, and accede adds what assent never carries: the sense that you resisted before finally giving way.

Agree is the plain, everyday word for any shared yes — you can agree with a friend, a plan, or a forecast, instantly and gladly. Accede is narrower and more formal: it answers a request or demand aimed at you, and it reports that you held out first.

For three years, the manager of the valley's radio station refused every request to rebroadcast the morning frost warnings in Spanish.
The growers' cooperative kept asking.
It sent letters, then signatures, then a delegation of orchard owners who sat politely in the lobby each harvest week.
This fall the station finally acceded: the warnings now run twice, in both languages, before dawn.
The manager is frank about the word.
He did not simply come around, he says — he was worn down, and the request was granted because holding out had stopped making sense.
The cooperative's president keeps one of the old refusal letters framed, dated three harvests back.
